What does an "Asynchronous" online program mean?

Step 1: Asynchronous learning means students and teachers do not have to be online at the same time for daily instruction. Students can log in and complete lessons and assignments at times that work for their schedule while still meeting Texas Tech K-12 academic, attendance and course-progress requirements.

Step 2: Teachers provide instruction, feedback and academic support throughout the course, but students are responsible for actively engaging with their coursework and staying on track.

Understanding the TSI Assessment Test

The current TSI Assessment test is version two, commonly referred to as TSIA2. TSIA2 was administered for any student taking the test after Jan. 11, 2021, and replaced the original TSI Assessment test (TSIA).

Before taking TSIA2, students are required to participate in a Pre-Assessment Activity. The activity will explain some of the test procedures and provide practice test questions along with feedback on answers to the practice questions. The activity also will provide options and campus resources to help them meet minimum standards.

The TSI Assessment in Mathematics contains a multiple-choice assessment with approximately 20 items on the placement test and 10 items in each section of the diagnostic test. Students with passing scores on the placement test will not be required to take the diagnostic test.

The TSI Assessment in Reading contains multiple choice with approximately 24 questions in the placement test and 10-12 items in each section of the diagnostic test.

The TSI Assessment in Writing contains a multiple-choice section and an essay section. There are approximately 24 items in the placement test and 10-12 items per section in the diagnostic test. For the essay section, students are asked to write a five-paragraph essay on an issue of current interest.

International Admission Requirements Texas Tech K-12

Texas Tech K-12 international students are those that do not hold U.S. Citizenship or Permanent residence and are studying outside of the United States. These students may provide the international undergraduate admissions office with unofficial documents for evaluation purposes. International students will be able to email unofficial Texas Tech K-12 transcripts with a Subject line: Fast-Track Texas Tech K-12 to internationals@ttu.edu. After all required documentation is received via email, a decision will be given within two business days via email. As long as the student meets the minimum GPA requirement of the university, the student will be automatically conditionally admitted.

For any questions regarding international admissions, you may reach out to Caitlyn English at caitlyn.english@ttu.edu.

International students who wish to continue with their admissions process, must fulfill the following application requirements:

Step 1: Complete an international application for admission through ApplyTexas Application or Common App or the TTU International Application.

Step 2: Pay a $75 non-refundable and non-waivable application fee.

Step 3: Provide English translations of official high school transcript(s) from the high school in their country, showing GPA and class rank; if the transcript does not have a rank one will be assigned.

Step 4: English Proficiency is waived for two years completed at a U.S. accredited high school; student must submit an official Texas Tech K-12 program transcript with two years completed.

Weighted Coursework

Eligible Advanced Placement (AP), Honors, International Baccalaureate (IB) and Dual Credit/Concurrent Credit courses receive additional GPA weight in accordance with Texas Tech K-12 policy.

Eligible transferred coursework with an approved weighted-course designation may also receive the corresponding GPA weight when applied toward Texas Tech High School graduation requirements.

Transfer Grades for the High School Program

Students transferring to Texas Tech High School from an accredited public or private school must provide an official transcript, report card or other required academic records for evaluation.

Texas Tech K-12 will review eligible coursework to determine which credits may be applied toward the student’s Texas Tech High School graduation requirements. Transfer grades from accredited schools are included in the student’s GPA unless the course is designated as local credit or graded on a pass/fail basis.

Students transferring from a homeschool program or non-accredited school or program must provide appropriate academic documentation, such as transcripts or grade reports, for review. Grades from homeschool or non-accredited programs are not directly transferable for credit. Students may earn applicable credit by completing the appropriate CBE or by enrolling in the corresponding course.

Texas Tech K-12 reserves the right to make the final determination regarding the acceptance and application of transferred coursework toward Texas Tech High School graduation requirements.

The following designations will receive weighted credits:

Step 1: Advanced Placement (AP) or Passing (P)

Step 2: Honors

Step 3: International Baccalaureate (IB)

Step 4: Dual Credit/Concurrent Credit

All accredited Texas Tech K-12 courses taken by a student that apply to graduation will be used to compute the Grade Point Average, excluding any approved Physical Education Substitution (SUBPRO) credits and local credit courses.

Texas Tech K-12 academic advisors will make every effort to assist students in transferring grades and credits from accredited public or private schools as allowed by Texas Education Agency (TEA) policies and Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS). answer.text:
**Withdrawal Processing Timeline for TTU K-12**

- Once a student submits a written request to withdraw from the full-time program, the request is processed by the Financial Services team.
- There is no specific number of days stated for the entire withdrawal process, but you should allow time for the administrative processing, which includes a $40.00 administration fee.
- After submitting your intent to withdraw, the process will begin as soon as your request is received.

**How to Submit a Withdrawal Request**
- Submit your intent to withdraw in writing through the Current Student Support portal: [Current Student Support (opens in new tab)](https://support.k12.ttu.edu/k12?id=report_issue&sys_id=043a96811b358e50239f0e1de54bcbeb)

**Important Notes**
- No refunds are allowed after the first 30 days of enrollment.
- If you are eligible for a refund, it will be processed after the withdrawal request is reviewed and approved.

**Next Step**
- Submit your withdrawal request via the support portal above and monitor your email for confirmation or further instructions from the Financial Services team.

For additional questions or to check the status of your withdrawal, you may contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.
